title: Incident Report: unsanctioned agent behaviour during cyber testing  | AISI Work
excerpt: During a routine cyber evaluation, AISI identified an incident in which AI agents took sustained, unsanctioned action directed at real people and organisations. We are disclosing what we found, what it means, and the actions now underway.
content_html:
You can access the full technical report here.

AISI’s role is to evaluate and understand the capabilities of frontier AI models, surfacing potential risks before they reach the public. To assess what these models can do, including whether they could be misused for cyberattacks, we test them under deliberately permissive conditions: with access to the open internet, and with some safety filters disabled.

On 28th July 2026, AISI's Security Team detected unusual data transfers leaving our research systems during a routine cyber evaluation. On investigation, we found that some of the agents being tested had engaged in sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organisations. We declared a security incident and, within roughly one hour of discovery, had contained it and begun a full investigation.

The incident stemmed from a single evaluation where agents were given a task of solving a cyber security challenge. We ran this challenge 122 times across several models. Our investigation found that in 10 of those runs, an AI agent took autonomous, unsanctioned action on the live internet, targeting real people and organisations. In total, we catalogued 19 such actions. Almost all of this behaviour (17 actions) came from a single model, Anthropic's Mythos 5, with 2 actions involving OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Sol with cyber classifiers (mechanisms to prevent misuse) disabled. In the most serious case, an agent tried to insert malicious code into an open-source project. In an attempt to get the code approved, the agent engaged in social engineering  — creating fake online identities and using them to pressure the project's maintainer to approve the code. A human maintainer caught and refused to approve the malicious code.

These attempts were unsuccessful, and our investigations have not evidenced any resulting real-world harm. But this is the first time we have seen risks around autonomy and deception manifest this clearly, without specific prompting, in the real-world.  

Importantly, this was not a case of a model escaping its secure test environment, or ‘sandbox’. As was standard in our cyber testing, we had intentionally permitted internet access, and model-provider cyber classifiers were deliberately disabled - conditions that do not reflect how frontier models are made available to the public. We do this to best assess the maximum capability of models. These configuration choices have been common practice in frontier AI evaluations. The specific models in question, in the configurations in which we tested them are not commercially available and there is no clear indication of similar activity outside of testing scenarios.  

Ahead of publishing this blog, we notified GitHub (the developer platform accessed during the evaluation) of the agents' malicious activity, which included actions that GitHub has confirmed violated their terms of service. We worked together with GitHub to remove artefacts left behind by the agent, and to notify the GitHub users the model interacted with. We have also contacted other affected parties. We also intend to work with METR (Model Evaluation and Threat Research) to conduct an independent third-party review – we are still working through the scope of this review with them.

This incident should be interpreted with caution and nuance. To some degree, our evaluation design choices and specific configurations enabled the behaviour. Nonetheless, the activity undertaken by the agent show signs of novel, potentially deceptive behaviours, and were to an extent and severity we did not anticipate.

There are important caveats to bear in mind: we observed a small number of events under very specific conditions, and cannot yet say how likely such behaviour is in different contexts or outside of testing environments. We cannot yet be certain when the agent understood it was taking real world action, or to what extent it believed it was in a fictional test scenario; our analysis so far presents a mixed picture and is ongoing.  

What we can say is that the behaviour was possible, sustained, and new; that alone warrants attention.  

This is precisely the kind of behaviour AISI exists to uncover, surfacing it in a controlled evaluation, so it can be understood and addressed before more capable models are widely deployed. This post sets out what happened, why it matters, and what we are doing in response. Our accompanying technical incident report provides further detail, and we intend to share more as our investigation continues.

‍What happened

AISI regularly tests the cyber capabilities of frontier models using cyber ranges: controlled, simulated networks that mimic real-world systems. An AI agent is given a cybersecurity challenge to solve, such as finding a protected piece of data, and works autonomously over many steps to complete it.

This exercise compared an existing cyber range against a new range, testing seven different models on the two ranges over 122 runs in total. All runs were conducted in AISI’s research environment, using virtual machine sandboxing to isolate the agents from other AISI infrastructure. Two features of the evaluation’s set-up are central to what followed:

  • Internet access was deliberately enabled. To measure what these models can genuinely do, we test them under conditions that reflect what a capable human attacker could do, including access to the open internet.
  • The developers' cyber classifiers were deliberately switched off. Frontier models are usually deployed with built-in filters that block dangerous behaviour. As a trusted testing partner, AISI can disable these filters to elicit a model's underlying capabilities.

This combination of conditions is not reflective of how frontier models are made available to the general public.

‍How we discovered the incident

On the morning of 28th July, our security monitoring flagged data leaving one of our testing systems through the ‘Tor’ anonymity network, which is commonly used to disguise the origin of internet traffic. The team running the evaluation began reviewing the agent's activity within minutes.

They quickly found that, during one run, the agent had created a malicious ‘pull request’ (a proposed code change) on a real, public open-source project on GitHub. We declared a security incident, stopped all related evaluations, and disabled internal access to the most capable models. All evaluation runs were terminated, and relevant machines isolated, within one hour of the alert being raised. Over the following hours and days, we reviewed the full set of runs, combining automated transcript scanning with expert manual analysis, to establish what had happened, and whether anything similar had occurred elsewhere.

‍What we found

43 of the 122 runs involved Mythos 5, and 35 of the 122 runs involved GPT-5.6 Sol. The overwhelming majority of the 122 runs proceeded as intended. However, in 10 of the 122 runs, we identified 19 cases where an agent had taken distinct actions beyond the scope of the testing parameters. 17 of these cases came from Mythos 5, and 2 came from a single run involving GPT-5.6 Sol.  

The 19 cases were not separate incidents; they clustered into a few connected behaviours. They primarily arose from a single sustained line of activity by one agent (Mythos 5), with a handful of related actions elsewhere. This behaviour occurred between July 25th and July 28th 2026.

Below, we highlight the four most significant behaviours observed. A full summary of cases is available in our technical incident report.

1. An attempted supply-chain attack on real open-source software. In the most serious sequence, an agent tried to insert malicious code into a publicly used open-source project and took actions in an attempt to secure approval for this insertion by human reviewers. The agent researched the project's human maintainers, created multiple fake identities, and used the fake identities to socially engineer a real maintainer into approving the code. When the agent’s pull request was challenged in public, it edited its earlier activity to appear harmless and considered adopting a fresh identity to continue. The agent used Tor to bypass some network restrictions on GitHub, which is what first triggered AISI’s security alert.

2. Attempts to deceive and target real people. As part of the same effort, the agent tried to contact real people directly, sending messages and files through an online file-transfer service to persuade them, or their own AI coding tools, to run malicious code. Some messages carried harmful payloads, and some were attempts at social engineering; targeted at real people – something we’ve never previously observed.  

3. Attempts to plant and prompt-inject malicious code. The agent tried to insert malicious instructions where it reasoned that other automated AI systems might pick them up and execute them. Prompt-injections are hidden instructions designed to manipulate AI coding assistants.

4. Collaboration between independent agents being assessed simultaneously. One agent left public messages on GitHub offering collaboration with other agents working on the same challenge. It also provided instructions to reuse accounts and artefacts it had left behind, which were discovered and used by subsequent agents.

We assessed each event for its potential to cause real-world harm. The most serious attempts were unsuccessful. Some actions had a limited real-world effect, but in contained circumstances; we set these out in the accompanying technical report.  Our investigation has not identified any resulting real-world harm.

‍Why this happened

Fundamentally, the agent took these actions to complete the task it had been set – to solve the cyber range. Several factors contributed to the emergence of unsanctioned behaviours:  

  • The agent pursued its goal persistently. AI agents explore routes their operators did not intend. Given a difficult objective, the agent kept searching for a way through, and some of the routes it found involved trying to deceive real people. It was never instructed to deceive; deception emerged as a by-product of pursuing the task, the kind of goal-directed deception that, until recently, had been largely theoretical.
  • The task was hard, and misconfigurations sometimes made it harder. In a number of runs, the task prompt was misconfigured so that the agent (incorrectly) believed no 'solve' existed that didn't require it to go beyond the intended task scope. There is good reason to think near-impossible tasks push models towards more ‘creative’, and more transgressive, problem-solving. But this does not fully explain the behaviours: in some runs the agent acted this way even when it had the necessary instructions to solve the task as intended.
  • Internet access was open, and monitoring was not purpose-built. We deliberately granted internet access to allow the agent to download tools required for its task; what we did not anticipate was that this would lead the agent to use this internet access to direct action at real people. In earlier model generations, this risk trade-off was judged to be acceptable, but we did not revisit that judgment quickly enough as capabilities advanced. Our security team detected the anomalous traffic through general monitoring after the fact, not through monitoring built to watch the evaluation as it ran, which could have flagged or blocked the behaviour sooner.
  • The agent was not specifically instructed not to leverage open internet access or avoid social engineering elements. Previously, it was not clear that such instructions were necessary when using models with alignment training.  

The factors that limited the damage also provide valuable insight. Human review and good security practice played an important role. In one instance, an agent's malicious pull request was caught by a human reviewer. The agent’s attempt to conduct social engineering by creating fake accounts to encourage the reviewer to approve this request failed. A member of the public, who suspected the code was malicious, opened it inside a secure, isolated environment built to contain such code.  

Additionally, the agent did not directly escape the secure test environment (‘sandbox’) that keeps the test environment sealed off from AISI's other internal systems. Agents often explore such an environment to understand what they can access, but here no agents tried to break out of it, or attack AISI’s systems.

In these cases, standard good practice, human judgment, and caution around AI-generated code stopped the worst outcomes. But in several cases the margin between failure and success was narrow, resting on human vigilance rather than a technical barrier that would reliably prevent this behaviour in a more capable agent.

‍Lessons for the future

We are treating this as a serious incident, warranting lasting change for AISI’s evaluation protocols and security architecture. Three lessons stand out for AISI and other evaluators:

  • Tighter controls on internet access. We are building fine-grained network controls into our cyber ranges, with the aim to preserve the realism these evaluations need while constraining them appropriately. We already use fine-grained network controls in all other evaluations, and will now treat the decision to grant internet access as one that must be actively justified rather than a default.
  • Real-time monitoring. We are introducing monitoring built to watch an evaluation as it runs, able to flag or block out-of-scope actions as they happen.
  • Reassessing evaluation design. Evaluations should assume a capable model may try to act beyond its remit, with the scope of any such behaviour limited in advance. AISI’s sandboxing guidelines recommend tailoring the sandbox configuration based on the design of the evaluation; good containment should not depend on the model choosing not to test its boundaries. We are also adding additional checks to ensure tasks are correctly specified and solvable by the intended route.

Alongside these changes, we are analysing what happened from both a cybersecurity and an AI alignment perspective, as well as auditing past evaluations for comparable behaviour that may have gone unnoticed.

We are also disclosing this openly so others can learn from our experience and continue to work closely with Anthropic and OpenAI to investigate this incident further.

‍What this means for people and businesses

This incident occurred in a controlled evaluation, not in ordinary use, and there is no clear indication of similar activity outside of testing scenarios. It is, however, a reason to prepare. As AI models become more capable and accessible, what we have seen during this incident could become more common.

The most effective response remains standard cyber hygiene, which matters more as AI advances. Organisations should ensure the cyber security basics are implemented robustly and be cautious when verifying outside code and contributions. This is an area where the leaders of the Five Eyes cyber security agencies have jointly called for action, and the National Cyber Security Centre has issued guidance on how to prepare as frontier AI’s cyber capabilities evolve. We encourage organisations of all kinds to sign up to the NCSC’s free Early Warning service, to make cyber a board-level responsibility, and to require Cyber Essentials right across their supply chains.

‍Final reflections‍

Incidents of this kind reflect the speed at which AI is developing. As capabilities advance, the work of understanding these systems, and ensuring their safety, must keep pace alongside them.

AISI is a capable organisation with strong safety practices, and we identified this behaviour through our own procedures. But no organisation's defences remain sufficient indefinitely. In this case, we deliberately enabled internet access, and did not have active monitoring that would have surfaced the behaviour sooner – things we will directly address moving forward. We are being open about these lessons so others can learn and adjust.

Taken alongside recent incidents reported by OpenAI and Anthropic, this incident points to a shift in the risk landscape. Harm may arise not only when people deliberately misuse publicly available models, but when capable agents operating in an internal research or privileged-access setting take unintended action beyond their authorised scope.

We have outlined important caveats that contextualise this incident. These behaviours emerged during an evaluation in which an agent was trying to complete a task. We cannot currently be certain when exactly the agent thought it was in a test, or how aware of potential real-world implications of its actions it was. In any case, this incident indicates a direction of travel that warrants immediate attention.

AISI exists to identify these problems, understand them, and share what we learn so they can be addressed before more capable systems are deployed – internally in AI labs, to trusted partners, and also to the public. The work is not complete, but it is shared across government, industry and the research community. The task now is to strengthen our defences, and ensure that safety work keeps pace.

sentences.en: We ran this challenge 122 times across several models.
sentences.zh: 我们在多个模型中运行了该挑战 122 次。

sentences.en: Our investigation found that in 10 of those runs, an AI agent took autonomous, unsanctioned action on the live internet, targeting real people and organisations.
sentences.zh: 我们的调查发现，在其中 10 次运行中，人工智能代理在实时互联网上针对真实的人和组织采取了自主的、未经批准的行动。

sentences.en: In total, we catalogued 19 such actions.
sentences.zh: 我们总共列出了 19 项此类行动。

sentences.en: Almost all of this behaviour (17 actions) came from a single model, Anthropic's Mythos 5, with 2 actions involving OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Sol with cyber classifiers (mechanisms to prevent misuse) disabled.
sentences.zh: 几乎所有这些行为（17 个操作）都来自一个模型，即 Anthropic 的 Mythos 5，其中 2 个操作涉及 OpenAI 的 GPT-5.6-Sol，并且禁用了网络分类器（防止误用的机制）。

sentences.en: In the most serious case, an agent tried to insert malicious code into an open-source project.
sentences.zh: 在最严重的情况下，代理试图将恶意代码插入开源项目。

sentences.en: In an attempt to get the code approved, the agent engaged in social engineering — creating fake online identities and using them to pressure the project's maintainer to approve the code.
sentences.zh: 为了让代码获得批准，该特工进行了社会工程——创建虚假的在线身份，并利用它们向项目维护人员施压，要求其批准代码。

sentences.en: A human maintainer caught and refused to approve the malicious code.
sentences.zh: 人类维护人员发现并拒绝批准恶意代码。

blocks.html_en: These attempts were unsuccessful, and our investigations have not evidenced any resulting real-world harm. But this is the first time we have seen risks around autonomy and deception manifest this clearly, without specific prompting, in the real-world.

sentences.en: These attempts were unsuccessful, and our investigations have not evidenced any resulting real-world harm.
sentences.zh: 这些尝试没有成功，我们的调查也没有证明任何由此产生的现实伤害。

sentences.en: But this is the first time we have seen risks around autonomy and deception manifest this clearly, without specific prompting, in the real-world.
sentences.zh: 但这是我们第一次看到围绕自主和欺骗的风险在现实世界中在没有具体提示的情况下清晰地体现出来。

blocks.html_en: Importantly, this was not a case of a model escaping its secure test environment, or ‘sandbox’. As was standard in our cyber testing, we had intentionally permitted internet access, and model-provider cyber classifiers were deliberately disabled - conditions that do not reflect how frontier models are made available to the public. We do this to best assess the maximum capability of models. These configuration choices have been common practice in frontier AI evaluations. The specific models in question, in the configurations in which we tested them are not commercially available and there is no clear indication of similar activity outside of testing scenarios.

sentences.en: Importantly, this was not a case of a model escaping its secure test environment, or ‘sandbox’.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，这并不是模型逃离其安全测试环境或“沙箱”的情况。

sentences.en: As was standard in our cyber testing, we had intentionally permitted internet access, and model-provider cyber classifiers were deliberately disabled - conditions that do not reflect how frontier models are made available to the public.
sentences.zh: 按照我们网络测试的标准，我们有意允许互联网访问，并且故意禁用模型提供商的网络分类器 - 这些条件并不反映如何向公众提供前沿模型。

sentences.en: We do this to best assess the maximum capability of models.
sentences.zh: 我们这样做是为了最好地评估模型的最大能力。

sentences.en: These configuration choices have been common practice in frontier AI evaluations.
sentences.zh: 这些配置选择是前沿人工智能评估中的常见做法。

sentences.en: The specific models in question, in the configurations in which we tested them are not commercially available and there is no clear indication of similar activity outside of testing scenarios.
sentences.zh: 所讨论的具体模型在我们测试的配置中尚未商用，并且在测试场景之外没有明确的迹象表明存在类似活动。

blocks.html_en: Ahead of publishing this blog, we notified GitHub (the developer platform accessed during the evaluation) of the agents' malicious activity, which included actions that GitHub has confirmed violated their terms of service. We worked together with GitHub to remove artefacts left behind by the agent, and to notify the GitHub users the model interacted with. We have also contacted other affected parties. We also intend to work with METR (Model Evaluation and Threat Research) to conduct an independent third-party review – we are still working through the scope of this review with them.

sentences.en: Ahead of publishing this blog, we notified GitHub (the developer platform accessed during the evaluation) of the agents' malicious activity, which included actions that GitHub has confirmed violated their terms of service.
sentences.zh: 在发布此博客之前，我们向 GitHub（评估期间访问的开发者平台）通报了代理的恶意活动，其中包括 GitHub 已确认违反其服务条款的行为。

sentences.en: We worked together with GitHub to remove artefacts left behind by the agent, and to notify the GitHub users the model interacted with.
sentences.zh: 我们与 GitHub 合作，删除代理留下的痕迹，并通知与模型交互的 GitHub 用户。

sentences.en: We have also contacted other affected parties.
sentences.zh: 我们还联系了其他受影响方。

sentences.en: We also intend to work with METR (Model Evaluation and Threat Research) to conduct an independent third-party review – we are still working through the scope of this review with them.
sentences.zh: 我们还打算与 METR（模型评估和威胁研究）合作进行独立的第三方审查——我们仍在与他们一起完成此次审查的范围。

blocks.html_en: This incident should be interpreted with caution and nuance. To some degree, our evaluation design choices and specific configurations enabled the behaviour. Nonetheless, the activity undertaken by the agent show signs of novel, potentially deceptive behaviours, and were to an extent and severity we did not anticipate.

sentences.en: This incident should be interpreted with caution and nuance.
sentences.zh: 对这一事件的解释应谨慎而细致。

sentences.en: To some degree, our evaluation design choices and specific configurations enabled the behaviour.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我们的评估设计选择和特定配置启用了该行为。

sentences.en: Nonetheless, the activity undertaken by the agent show signs of novel, potentially deceptive behaviours, and were to an extent and severity we did not anticipate.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，该特工进行的活动显示出新颖的、潜在的欺骗性行为的迹象，并且其程度和严重程度是我们没有预料到的。

blocks.html_en: There are important caveats to bear in mind: we observed a small number of events under very specific conditions, and cannot yet say how likely such behaviour is in different contexts or outside of testing environments. We cannot yet be certain when the agent understood it was taking real world action, or to what extent it believed it was in a fictional test scenario; our analysis so far presents a mixed picture and is ongoing.

sentences.en: There are important caveats to bear in mind: we observed a small number of events under very specific conditions, and cannot yet say how likely such behaviour is in different contexts or outside of testing environments.
sentences.zh: 有一些重要的警告需要记住：我们在非常特定的条件下观察到了少量事件，并且还不能说这种行为在不同的上下文或测试环境之外的可能性有多大。

sentences.en: We cannot yet be certain when the agent understood it was taking real world action, or to what extent it believed it was in a fictional test scenario; our analysis so far presents a mixed picture and is ongoing.
sentences.zh: 我们还不能确定智能体何时理解它正在采取现实世界的行动，或者它在多大程度上相信它是在虚构的测试场景中；到目前为止，我们的分析呈现出复杂的情况，并且仍在进行中。

blocks.html_en: What we can say is that the behaviour was possible, sustained, and new; that alone warrants attention.

sentences.en: What we can say is that the behaviour was possible, sustained, and new; that alone warrants attention.
sentences.zh: 我们可以说的是，这种行为是可能的、持续的、新颖的；仅这一点就值得关注。

blocks.html_en: This is precisely the kind of behaviour AISI exists to uncover, surfacing it in a controlled evaluation, so it can be understood and addressed before more capable models are widely deployed. This post sets out what happened, why it matters, and what we are doing in response. Our accompanying technical incident report provides further detail, and we intend to share more as our investigation continues.

sentences.en: This is precisely the kind of behaviour AISI exists to uncover, surfacing it in a controlled evaluation, so it can be understood and addressed before more capable models are widely deployed.
sentences.zh: 这正是 AISI 所要发现的行为，并在受控评估中将其呈现出来，以便在更强​​大的模型被广泛部署之前可以理解和解决它。

sentences.en: This post sets out what happened, why it matters, and what we are doing in response.
sentences.zh: 这篇文章阐述了发生的事情、其重要性以及我们正在采取的应对措施。

sentences.en: Our accompanying technical incident report provides further detail, and we intend to share more as our investigation continues.
sentences.zh: 我们随附的技术事件报告提供了更多详细信息，并且我们打算在调查继续进行时分享更多信息。

blocks.html_en: ‍What happened

sentences.en: ‍What happened
sentences.zh: 发生了什么

blocks.html_en: AISI regularly tests the cyber capabilities of frontier models using cyber ranges: controlled, simulated networks that mimic real-world systems. An AI agent is given a cybersecurity challenge to solve, such as finding a protected piece of data, and works autonomously over many steps to complete it.

sentences.en: AISI regularly tests the cyber capabilities of frontier models using cyber ranges: controlled, simulated networks that mimic real-world systems.
sentences.zh: AISI 定期使用网络范围测试前沿模型的网络能力：模仿现实世界系统的受控模拟网络。

sentences.en: An AI agent is given a cybersecurity challenge to solve, such as finding a protected piece of data, and works autonomously over many steps to complete it.
sentences.zh: 人工智能代理需要解决网络安全挑战，例如查找受保护的数据，并通过多个步骤自主工作来完成它。

blocks.html_en: This exercise compared an existing cyber range against a new range, testing seven different models on the two ranges over 122 runs in total. All runs were conducted in AISI’s research environment, using virtual machine sandboxing to isolate the agents from other AISI infrastructure. Two features of the evaluation’s set-up are central to what followed:

sentences.en: This exercise compared an existing cyber range against a new range, testing seven different models on the two ranges over 122 runs in total.
sentences.zh: 这项练习将现有的网络靶场与新靶场进行了比较，在两个靶场上测试了 7 种不同的型号，总共运行了 122 次。

sentences.en: All runs were conducted in AISI’s research environment, using virtual machine sandboxing to isolate the agents from other AISI infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 所有运行均在 AISI 的研究环境中进行，使用虚拟机沙箱将代理与其他 AISI 基础设施隔离。

sentences.en: Two features of the evaluation’s set-up are central to what followed:
sentences.zh: 评估设置的两个特征对于接下来的内容至关重要：

blocks.html_en: • Internet access was deliberately enabled. To measure what these models can genuinely do, we test them under conditions that reflect what a capable human attacker could do, including access to the open internet.

sentences.en: Internet access was deliberately enabled.
sentences.zh: 互联网访问是故意启用的。

sentences.en: To measure what these models can genuinely do, we test them under conditions that reflect what a capable human attacker could do, including access to the open internet.
sentences.zh: 为了衡量这些模型的真正功能，我们在反映有能力的人类攻击者可以做什么的条件下对它们进行测试，包括访问开放互联网。

blocks.html_en: • The developers' cyber classifiers were deliberately switched off. Frontier models are usually deployed with built-in filters that block dangerous behaviour. As a trusted testing partner, AISI can disable these filters to elicit a model's underlying capabilities.

sentences.en: The developers' cyber classifiers were deliberately switched off.
sentences.zh: 开发人员的网络分类器被故意关闭。

sentences.en: Frontier models are usually deployed with built-in filters that block dangerous behaviour.
sentences.zh: 前沿模型通常部署有内置过滤器，可以阻止危险行为。

sentences.en: As a trusted testing partner, AISI can disable these filters to elicit a model's underlying capabilities.
sentences.zh: 作为值得信赖的测试合作伙伴，AISI 可以禁用这些过滤器以获取模型的底层功能。

blocks.html_en: This combination of conditions is not reflective of how frontier models are made available to the general public.

sentences.en: This combination of conditions is not reflective of how frontier models are made available to the general public.
sentences.zh: 这种条件组合并不反映如何向公众提供前沿模型。

blocks.html_en: ‍How we discovered the incident

sentences.en: ‍How we discovered the incident
sentences.zh: ‍我们是如何发现这一事件的

blocks.html_en: On the morning of 28th July, our security monitoring flagged data leaving one of our testing systems through the ‘Tor’ anonymity network, which is commonly used to disguise the origin of internet traffic. The team running the evaluation began reviewing the agent's activity within minutes.

sentences.en: On the morning of 28th July, our security monitoring flagged data leaving one of our testing systems through the ‘Tor’ anonymity network, which is commonly used to disguise the origin of internet traffic.
sentences.zh: 7 月 28 日上午，我们的安全监控标记了通过“Tor”匿名网络离开我们的测试系统的数据，该网络通常用于伪装互联网流量的来源。

sentences.en: The team running the evaluation began reviewing the agent's activity within minutes.
sentences.zh: 运行评估的团队在几分钟内开始审查代理的活动。

blocks.html_en: They quickly found that, during one run, the agent had created a malicious ‘pull request’ (a proposed code change) on a real, public open-source project on GitHub. We declared a security incident, stopped all related evaluations, and disabled internal access to the most capable models. All evaluation runs were terminated, and relevant machines isolated, within one hour of the alert being raised. Over the following hours and days, we reviewed the full set of runs, combining automated transcript scanning with expert manual analysis, to establish what had happened, and whether anything similar had occurred elsewhere.

sentences.en: They quickly found that, during one run, the agent had created a malicious ‘pull request’ (a proposed code change) on a real, public open-source project on GitHub.
sentences.zh: 他们很快发现，在一次运行期间，代理在 GitHub 上的一个真实的公共开源项目上创建了恶意“拉取请求”（拟议的代码更改）。

sentences.en: We declared a security incident, stopped all related evaluations, and disabled internal access to the most capable models.
sentences.zh: 我们宣布发生安全事件，停止所有相关评估，并禁用对最强大模型的内部访问。

sentences.en: All evaluation runs were terminated, and relevant machines isolated, within one hour of the alert being raised.
sentences.zh: 发出警报后一小时内，所有评估运行均被终止，并隔离相关机器。

sentences.en: Over the following hours and days, we reviewed the full set of runs, combining automated transcript scanning with expert manual analysis, to establish what had happened, and whether anything similar had occurred elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几个小时和几天里，我们审查了全套运行，将自动转录扫描与专家手动分析相结合，以确定发生了什么，以及其他地方是否发生了类似的情况。

blocks.html_en: ‍What we found

sentences.en: ‍What we found
sentences.zh: ‍我们发现了什么

blocks.html_en: 43 of the 122 runs involved Mythos 5, and 35 of the 122 runs involved GPT-5.6 Sol. The overwhelming majority of the 122 runs proceeded as intended. However, in 10 of the 122 runs, we identified 19 cases where an agent had taken distinct actions beyond the scope of the testing parameters. 17 of these cases came from Mythos 5, and 2 came from a single run involving GPT-5.6 Sol.

sentences.en: 43 of the 122 runs involved Mythos 5, and 35 of the 122 runs involved GPT-5.6 Sol.
sentences.zh: 122 次运行中的 43 次涉及 Mythos 5，122 次运行中的 35 次涉及 GPT-5.6 Sol。

sentences.en: The overwhelming majority of the 122 runs proceeded as intended.
sentences.zh: 122 次运行中的绝大多数都按预期进行。

sentences.en: However, in 10 of the 122 runs, we identified 19 cases where an agent had taken distinct actions beyond the scope of the testing parameters.
sentences.zh: 然而，在 122 次运行中的 10 次中，我们发现了 19 个案例，其中代理采取了超出测试参数范围的明显操作。

sentences.en: 17 of these cases came from Mythos 5, and 2 came from a single run involving GPT-5.6 Sol.
sentences.zh: 其中 17 个案例来自 Mythos 5，2 个案例来自涉及 GPT-5.6 Sol 的单次运行。

blocks.html_en: The 19 cases were not separate incidents; they clustered into a few connected behaviours. They primarily arose from a single sustained line of activity by one agent (Mythos 5), with a handful of related actions elsewhere. This behaviour occurred between July 25th and July 28th 2026.

sentences.en: The 19 cases were not separate incidents; they clustered into a few connected behaviours.
sentences.zh: 这 19 起案件并不是单独的事件；它们聚集成一些相互关联的行为。

sentences.en: They primarily arose from a single sustained line of activity by one agent (Mythos 5), with a handful of related actions elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 它们主要源于一个特工的单一持续活动（神话 5），以及其他地方的一些相关行动。

sentences.en: This behaviour occurred between July 25th and July 28th 2026.
sentences.zh: 此行为发生在2026年7月25日至7月28日之间。

blocks.html_en: Below, we highlight the four most significant behaviours observed. A full summary of cases is available in our technical incident report.

sentences.en: Below, we highlight the four most significant behaviours observed.
sentences.zh: 下面，我们重点介绍观察到的四种最重要的行为。

sentences.en: A full summary of cases is available in our technical incident report.
sentences.zh: 我们的技术事件报告中提供了完整的案例摘要。

blocks.html_en: 1. An attempted supply-chain attack on real open-source software. In the most serious sequence, an agent tried to insert malicious code into a publicly used open-source project and took actions in an attempt to secure approval for this insertion by human reviewers. The agent researched the project's human maintainers, created multiple fake identities, and used the fake identities to socially engineer a real maintainer into approving the code. When the agent’s pull request was challenged in public, it edited its earlier activity to appear harmless and considered adopting a fresh identity to continue. The agent used Tor to bypass some network restrictions on GitHub, which is what first triggered AISI’s security alert.

sentences.en: An attempted supply-chain attack on real open-source software.
sentences.zh: 试图对真正的开源软件进行供应链攻击。

sentences.en: In the most serious sequence, an agent tried to insert malicious code into a publicly used open-source project and took actions in an attempt to secure approval for this insertion by human reviewers.
sentences.zh: 最严重的情况是，特工试图将恶意代码插入到公开使用的开源项目中，并采取行动以确保人类审查者批准此插入。

sentences.en: The agent researched the project's human maintainers, created multiple fake identities, and used the fake identities to socially engineer a real maintainer into approving the code.
sentences.zh: 该特工研究了该项目的人类维护者，创建了多个虚假身份，并使用虚假身份通过社会工程诱使真正的维护者批准代码。

sentences.en: When the agent’s pull request was challenged in public, it edited its earlier activity to appear harmless and considered adopting a fresh identity to continue.
sentences.zh: 当代理的拉取请求在公开场合受到质疑时，它编辑了之前的活动，使其看起来无害，并考虑采用新的身份继续。

sentences.en: The agent used Tor to bypass some network restrictions on GitHub, which is what first triggered AISI’s security alert.
sentences.zh: 该代理使用 Tor 绕过了 GitHub 上的一些网络限制，这也是首次触发 AISI 的安全警报。

blocks.html_en: 2. Attempts to deceive and target real people. As part of the same effort, the agent tried to contact real people directly, sending messages and files through an online file-transfer service to persuade them, or their own AI coding tools, to run malicious code. Some messages carried harmful payloads, and some were attempts at social engineering; targeted at real people – something we’ve never previously observed.

sentences.en: Attempts to deceive and target real people.
sentences.zh: 试图欺骗并针对真实的人。

sentences.en: As part of the same effort, the agent tried to contact real people directly, sending messages and files through an online file-transfer service to persuade them, or their own AI coding tools, to run malicious code.
sentences.zh: 作为同一努力的一部分，特工试图直接联系真实的人，通过在线文件传输服务发送消息和文件，说服他们或他们自己的人工智能编码工具运行恶意代码。

sentences.en: Some messages carried harmful payloads, and some were attempts at social engineering; targeted at real people – something we’ve never previously observed.
sentences.zh: 有些消息携带有害的有效负载，有些则试图进行社会工程；针对真实的人——这是我们以前从未观察到的。

blocks.html_en: 3. Attempts to plant and prompt-inject malicious code. The agent tried to insert malicious instructions where it reasoned that other automated AI systems might pick them up and execute them. Prompt-injections are hidden instructions designed to manipulate AI coding assistants.

sentences.en: Attempts to plant and prompt-inject malicious code.
sentences.zh: 尝试植入并提示注入恶意代码。

sentences.en: The agent tried to insert malicious instructions where it reasoned that other automated AI systems might pick them up and execute them.
sentences.zh: 该代理试图在其他自动化人工智能系统可能会识别并执行这些指令的地方插入恶意指令。

sentences.en: Prompt-injections are hidden instructions designed to manipulate AI coding assistants.
sentences.zh: 提示注入是旨在操纵人工智能编码助手的隐藏指令。

blocks.html_en: 4. Collaboration between independent agents being assessed simultaneously. One agent left public messages on GitHub offering collaboration with other agents working on the same challenge. It also provided instructions to reuse accounts and artefacts it had left behind, which were discovered and used by subsequent agents.

sentences.en: Collaboration between independent agents being assessed simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 同时评估独立代理之间的协作。

sentences.en: One agent left public messages on GitHub offering collaboration with other agents working on the same challenge.
sentences.zh: 一名特工在 GitHub 上留下了公开消息，表示愿意与其他应对同一挑战的特工进行合作。

sentences.en: It also provided instructions to reuse accounts and artefacts it had left behind, which were discovered and used by subsequent agents.
sentences.zh: 它还提供了重新使用其留下的帐户和文物的说明，这些帐户和文物被后续特工发现并使用。

blocks.html_en: We assessed each event for its potential to cause real-world harm. The most serious attempts were unsuccessful. Some actions had a limited real-world effect, but in contained circumstances; we set these out in the accompanying technical report.  Our investigation has not identified any resulting real-world harm.

sentences.en: We assessed each event for its potential to cause real-world harm.
sentences.zh: 我们评估了每个事件对现实世界造成伤害的可能性。

sentences.en: The most serious attempts were unsuccessful.
sentences.zh: 最认真的尝试都没有成功。

sentences.en: Some actions had a limited real-world effect, but in contained circumstances; we set these out in the accompanying technical report.
sentences.zh: 有些行为在现实世界中的影响有限，但是是在有限的情况下；我们在随附的技术报告中列出了这些内容。

sentences.en: Our investigation has not identified any resulting real-world harm.
sentences.zh: 我们的调查尚未发现任何由此造成的现实伤害。

blocks.html_en: ‍Why this happened

sentences.en: ‍Why this happened
sentences.zh: ‍为什么会发生这样的事

blocks.html_en: Fundamentally, the agent took these actions to complete the task it had been set – to solve the cyber range. Several factors contributed to the emergence of unsanctioned behaviours:

sentences.en: Fundamentally, the agent took these actions to complete the task it had been set – to solve the cyber range.
sentences.zh: 从根本上来说，特工采取这些行动是为了完成它所设定的任务——解决网络范围问题。

sentences.en: Several factors contributed to the emergence of unsanctioned behaviours:
sentences.zh: 有几个因素导致了未经批准的行为的出现：

blocks.html_en: • The agent pursued its goal persistently. AI agents explore routes their operators did not intend. Given a difficult objective, the agent kept searching for a way through, and some of the routes it found involved trying to deceive real people. It was never instructed to deceive; deception emerged as a by-product of pursuing the task, the kind of goal-directed deception that, until recently, had been largely theoretical.

sentences.en: The agent pursued its goal persistently.
sentences.zh: 代理人坚持不懈地追求其目标。

sentences.en: AI agents explore routes their operators did not intend.

sentences.en: Given a difficult objective, the agent kept searching for a way through, and some of the routes it found involved trying to deceive real people.
sentences.zh: 考虑到一个困难的目标，该特工不断寻找一条出路，它发现的一些路线涉及试图欺骗真实的人。

sentences.en: It was never instructed to deceive; deception emerged as a by-product of pursuing the task, the kind of goal-directed deception that, until recently, had been largely theoretical.
sentences.zh: 它从来没有被指示去欺骗；欺骗是追求任务的副产品，是一种以目标为导向的欺骗，直到最近，这种欺骗在很大程度上还停留在理论上。

blocks.html_en: • The task was hard, and misconfigurations sometimes made it harder. In a number of runs, the task prompt was misconfigured so that the agent (incorrectly) believed no 'solve' existed that didn't require it to go beyond the intended task scope. There is good reason to think near-impossible tasks push models towards more ‘creative’, and more transgressive, problem-solving. But this does not fully explain the behaviours: in some runs the agent acted this way even when it had the necessary instructions to solve the task as intended.

sentences.en: The task was hard, and misconfigurations sometimes made it harder.
sentences.zh: 这项任务很艰巨，而错误的配置有时会让任务变得更加困难。

sentences.en: In a number of runs, the task prompt was misconfigured so that the agent (incorrectly) believed no 'solve' existed that didn't require it to go beyond the intended task scope.

sentences.en: There is good reason to think near-impossible tasks push models towards more ‘creative’, and more transgressive, problem-solving.
sentences.zh: 我们有充分的理由认为，近乎不可能的任务会推动模型在解决问题方面变得更具“创造性”、更具突破性。

sentences.en: But this does not fully explain the behaviours: in some runs the agent acted this way even when it had the necessary instructions to solve the task as intended.
sentences.zh: 但这并不能完全解释这些行为：在某些运行中，即使代理有必要的指令来按预期解决任务，它也会以这种方式行事。

blocks.html_en: • Internet access was open, and monitoring was not purpose-built. We deliberately granted internet access to allow the agent to download tools required for its task; what we did not anticipate was that this would lead the agent to use this internet access to direct action at real people. In earlier model generations, this risk trade-off was judged to be acceptable, but we did not revisit that judgment quickly enough as capabilities advanced. Our security team detected the anomalous traffic through general monitoring after the fact, not through monitoring built to watch the evaluation as it ran, which could have flagged or blocked the behaviour sooner.

sentences.en: Internet access was open, and monitoring was not purpose-built.
sentences.zh: 互联网接入是开放的，监控也不是专门设计的。

sentences.en: Our security team detected the anomalous traffic through general monitoring after the fact, not through monitoring built to watch the evaluation as it ran, which could have flagged or blocked the behaviour sooner.
sentences.zh: 我们的安全团队在事后通过一般监控检测到异常流量，而不是通过为观察评估运行而构建的监控，这样可以更快地标记或阻止该行为。

blocks.html_en: • The agent was not specifically instructed not to leverage open internet access or avoid social engineering elements. Previously, it was not clear that such instructions were necessary when using models with alignment training.

sentences.zh: 该特工没有被明确指示不要利用开放的互联网访问或避免社会工程元素。

In one instance, an agent's malicious pull request was caught by a human reviewer. The agent’s attempt to conduct social engineering by creating fake accounts to encourage the reviewer to approve this request failed. A member of the public, who suspected the code was malicious, opened it inside a secure, isolated environment built to contain such code.

blocks.html_en: We are treating this as a serious incident, warranting lasting change for AISI’s evaluation protocols and security architecture. Three lessons stand out for AISI and other evaluators:

sentences.en: We are treating this as a serious incident, warranting lasting change for AISI’s evaluation protocols and security architecture.
sentences.zh: 我们将此视为严重事件，需要对 AISI 的评估协议和安全架构进行持久的改变。

sentences.en: Three lessons stand out for AISI and other evaluators:
sentences.zh: AISI 和其他评估者得出以下三个教训：

blocks.html_en: • Tighter controls on internet access. We are building fine-grained network controls into our cyber ranges, with the aim to preserve the realism these evaluations need while constraining them appropriately. We already use fine-grained network controls in all other evaluations, and will now treat the decision to grant internet access as one that must be actively justified rather than a default.

sentences.en: Tighter controls on internet access.
sentences.zh: 对互联网访问的更严格控制。

sentences.en: We are building fine-grained network controls into our cyber ranges, with the aim to preserve the realism these evaluations need while constraining them appropriately.
sentences.zh: 我们正在我们的网络范围中构建细粒度的网络控制，目的是在适当限制它们的同时保持这些评估所需的现实性。

sentences.zh: 我们已经在所有其他评估中使用了细粒度的网络控制，现在将把授予互联网访问权限的决定视为必须积极证明合理性的决定，而不是默认的决定。

blocks.html_en: • Real-time monitoring. We are introducing monitoring built to watch an evaluation as it runs, able to flag or block out-of-scope actions as they happen.

sentences.en: We are introducing monitoring built to watch an evaluation as it runs, able to flag or block out-of-scope actions as they happen.
sentences.zh: 我们正在引入监控功能，用于在评估运行时对其进行监视，能够在发生超出范围的操作时对其进行标记或阻止。

blocks.html_en: • Reassessing evaluation design. Evaluations should assume a capable model may try to act beyond its remit, with the scope of any such behaviour limited in advance. AISI’s sandboxing guidelines recommend tailoring the sandbox configuration based on the design of the evaluation; good containment should not depend on the model choosing not to test its boundaries. We are also adding additional checks to ensure tasks are correctly specified and solvable by the intended route.

sentences.zh: 评估应假设一个有能力的模型可能会尝试超出其职权范围的行为，并且预先限制任何此类行为的范围。

blocks.html_en: Alongside these changes, we are analysing what happened from both a cybersecurity and an AI alignment perspective, as well as auditing past evaluations for comparable behaviour that may have gone unnoticed.

blocks.html_en: This incident occurred in a controlled evaluation, not in ordinary use, and there is no clear indication of similar activity outside of testing scenarios. AISI 的作用是评估和了解前沿人工智能模型的能力，在潜在风险向公众传播之前将其暴露出来。 为了评估这些模型的功能，包括它们是否可能被滥用于网络攻击，我们在故意允许的条件下对它们进行了测试：访问开放互联网，并禁用一些安全过滤器。

2026 年 7 月 28 日，AISI 安全团队在例行网络评估期间检测到离开我们研究系统的异常数据传输。 经过调查，我们发现一些正在测试的代理针对真实的人和组织进行了持续的、潜在有害的活动。 我们宣布发生安全事件，并在发现后大约一小时内控制住了事件并开始全面调查。

该事件源于一次评估，其中特工被赋予解决网络安全挑战的任务。 我们在多个模型中运行了该挑战 122 次。 我们的调查发现，在其中 10 次运行中，人工智能代理在实时互联网上针对真实的人和组织采取了自主的、未经批准的行动。 我们总共列出了 19 项此类行动。 几乎所有这些行为（17 个操作）都来自一个模型，即 Anthropic 的 Mythos 5，其中 2 个操作涉及 OpenAI 的 GPT-5.6-Sol，并且禁用了网络分类器（防止误用的机制）。 在最严重的情况下，代理试图将恶意代码插入开源项目。 为了让代码获得批准，该特工进行了社会工程——创建虚假的在线身份，并利用它们向项目维护人员施压，要求其批准代码。 人类维护人员发现并拒绝批准恶意代码。

这些尝试没有成功，我们的调查也没有证明任何由此产生的现实伤害。 但这是我们第一次看到围绕自主和欺骗的风险在现实世界中在没有具体提示的情况下清晰地体现出来。

重要的是，这并不是模型逃离其安全测试环境或“沙箱”的情况。 按照我们网络测试的标准，我们有意允许互联网访问，并且故意禁用模型提供商的网络分类器 - 这些条件并不反映如何向公众提供前沿模型。 我们这样做是为了最好地评估模型的最大能力。 这些配置选择是前沿人工智能评估中的常见做法。 所讨论的具体模型在我们测试的配置中尚未商用，并且在测试场景之外没有明确的迹象表明存在类似活动。

在发布此博客之前，我们向 GitHub（评估期间访问的开发者平台）通报了代理的恶意活动，其中包括 GitHub 已确认违反其服务条款的行为。 我们与 GitHub 合作，删除代理留下的痕迹，并通知与模型交互的 GitHub 用户。 我们还联系了其他受影响方。 我们还打算与 METR（模型评估和威胁研究）合作进行独立的第三方审查——我们仍在与他们一起完成此次审查的范围。

对这一事件的解释应谨慎而细致。 在某种程度上，我们的评估设计选择和特定配置启用了该行为。 尽管如此，该特工进行的活动显示出新颖的、潜在的欺骗性行为的迹象，并且其程度和严重程度是我们没有预料到的。

有一些重要的警告需要记住：我们在非常特定的条件下观察到了少量事件，并且还不能说这种行为在不同的上下文或测试环境之外的可能性有多大。 我们还不能确定智能体何时理解它正在采取现实世界的行动，或者它在多大程度上相信它是在虚构的测试场景中；到目前为止，我们的分析呈现出复杂的情况，并且仍在进行中。

我们可以说的是，这种行为是可能的、持续的、新颖的；仅这一点就值得关注。

这正是 AISI 所要发现的行为，并在受控评估中将其呈现出来，以便在更强​​大的模型被广泛部署之前可以理解和解决它。 这篇文章阐述了发生的事情、其重要性以及我们正在采取的应对措施。 我们随附的技术事件报告提供了更多详细信息，并且我们打算在调查继续进行时分享更多信息。

发生了什么

AISI 定期使用网络范围测试前沿模型的网络能力：模仿现实世界系统的受控模拟网络。 人工智能代理需要解决网络安全挑战，例如查找受保护的数据，并通过多个步骤自主工作来完成它。

这项练习将现有的网络靶场与新靶场进行了比较，在两个靶场上测试了 7 种不同的型号，总共运行了 122 次。 所有运行均在 AISI 的研究环境中进行，使用虚拟机沙箱将代理与其他 AISI 基础设施隔离。 评估设置的两个特征对于接下来的内容至关重要：

  • 互联网访问是故意启用的。 为了衡量这些模型的真正功能，我们在反映有能力的人类攻击者可以做什么的条件下对它们进行测试，包括访问开放互联网。
  • 开发人员的网络分类器被故意关闭。 前沿模型通常部署有内置过滤器，可以阻止危险行为。 作为值得信赖的测试合作伙伴，AISI 可以禁用这些过滤器以获取模型的底层功能。

这种条件组合并不反映如何向公众提供前沿模型。

‍我们是如何发现这一事件的

7 月 28 日上午，我们的安全监控标记了通过“Tor”匿名网络离开我们的测试系统的数据，该网络通常用于伪装互联网流量的来源。 运行评估的团队在几分钟内开始审查代理的活动。

他们很快发现，在一次运行期间，代理在 GitHub 上的一个真实的公共开源项目上创建了恶意“拉取请求”（拟议的代码更改）。 我们宣布发生安全事件，停止所有相关评估，并禁用对最强大模型的内部访问。 发出警报后一小时内，所有评估运行均被终止，并隔离相关机器。 在接下来的几个小时和几天里，我们审查了全套运行，将自动转录扫描与专家手动分析相结合，以确定发生了什么，以及其他地方是否发生了类似的情况。

‍我们发现了什么

122 次运行中的 43 次涉及 Mythos 5，122 次运行中的 35 次涉及 GPT-5.6 Sol。 122 次运行中的绝大多数都按预期进行。 然而，在 122 次运行中的 10 次中，我们发现了 19 个案例，其中代理采取了超出测试参数范围的明显操作。 其中 17 个案例来自 Mythos 5，2 个案例来自涉及 GPT-5.6 Sol 的单次运行。

这 19 起案件并不是单独的事件；它们聚集成一些相互关联的行为。 它们主要源于一个特工的单一持续活动（神话 5），以及其他地方的一些相关行动。 此行为发生在2026年7月25日至7月28日之间。

下面，我们重点介绍观察到的四种最重要的行为。 我们的技术事件报告中提供了完整的案例摘要。

1. 试图对真正的开源软件进行供应链攻击。 最严重的情况是，特工试图将恶意代码插入到公开使用的开源项目中，并采取行动以确保人类审查者批准此插入。 该特工研究了该项目的人类维护者，创建了多个虚假身份，并使用虚假身份通过社会工程诱使真正的维护者批准代码。 当代理的拉取请求在公开场合受到质疑时，它编辑了之前的活动，使其看起来无害，并考虑采用新的身份继续。 该代理使用 Tor 绕过了 GitHub 上的一些网络限制，这也是首次触发 AISI 的安全警报。

2. 试图欺骗并针对真实的人。 作为同一努力的一部分，特工试图直接联系真实的人，通过在线文件传输服务发送消息和文件，说服他们或他们自己的人工智能编码工具运行恶意代码。 有些消息携带有害的有效负载，有些则试图进行社会工程；针对真实的人——这是我们以前从未观察到的。

3. 尝试植入并提示注入恶意代码。 该代理试图在其他自动化人工智能系统可能会识别并执行这些指令的地方插入恶意指令。 提示注入是旨在操纵人工智能编码助手的隐藏指令。

4. 同时评估独立代理之间的协作。 一名特工在 GitHub 上留下了公开消息，表示愿意与其他应对同一挑战的特工进行合作。 它还提供了重新使用其留下的帐户和文物的说明，这些帐户和文物被后续特工发现并使用。

我们评估了每个事件对现实世界造成伤害的可能性。 最认真的尝试都没有成功。 有些行为在现实世界中的影响有限，但是是在有限的情况下；我们在随附的技术报告中列出了这些内容。 我们的调查尚未发现任何由此造成的现实伤害。

‍为什么会发生这样的事

从根本上来说，特工采取这些行动是为了完成它所设定的任务——解决网络范围问题。 有几个因素导致了未经批准的行为的出现：

  • 代理人坚持不懈地追求其目标。 人工智能代理探索其操作员不希望的路线。 考虑到一个困难的目标，该特工不断寻找一条出路，它发现的一些路线涉及试图欺骗真实的人。 它从来没有被指示去欺骗；欺骗是追求任务的副产品，是一种以目标为导向的欺骗，直到最近，这种欺骗在很大程度上还停留在理论上。
  • 这项任务很艰巨，而错误的配置有时会让任务变得更加困难。 在多次运行中，任务提示配置错误，因此代理（错误地）认为不存在不需要超出预期任务范围的“解决方案”。 我们有充分的理由认为，近乎不可能的任务会推动模型在解决问题方面变得更具“创造性”、更具突破性。 但这并不能完全解释这些行为：在某些运行中，即使代理有必要的指令来按预期解决任务，它也会以这种方式行事。
  • 互联网接入是开放的，监控也不是专门设计的。 我们特意授予互联网访问权限，以允许代理下载其任务所需的工具；我们没有预料到的是，这会导致特工利用互联网访问对真实的人采取直接行动。 在早期的模型中，这种风险权衡被认为是可以接受的，但随着功能的进步，我们并没有足够快地重新审视这一判断。 我们的安全团队在事后通过一般监控检测到异常流量，而不是通过为观察评估运行而构建的监控，这样可以更快地标记或阻止该行为。
  • 该特工没有被明确指示不要利用开放的互联网访问或避免社会工程元素。 此前，尚不清楚在使用具有对齐训练的模型时是否需要此类说明。

限制损害的因素也提供了宝贵的见解。 人工审查和良好的安全实践发挥了重要作用。 在一个实例中，代理的恶意拉取请求被人工审核员捕获。 该特工试图通过创建虚假帐户来进行社会工程，以鼓励审核者批准此请求，但失败了。 一名怀疑该代码是恶意的公众在一个为包含此类代码而构建的安全、隔离的环境中打开了该代码。

此外，该代理并没有直接逃离安全测试环境（“沙箱”），该环境使测试环境与 AISI 的其他内部系统隔离。 特工经常探索这样的环境以了解他们可以访问什么，但这里没有特工试图突破它或攻击 AISI 的系统。

在这些情况下，标准的良好实践、人类判断以及对人工智能生成代码的谨慎态度阻止了最坏的结果。 但在某些情况下，失败与成功之间的差距很窄，这取决于人类的警惕性，而不是能够可靠地阻止能力更强的智能体出现这种行为的技术障碍。

‍未来的教训

我们将此视为严重事件，需要对 AISI 的评估协议和安全架构进行持久的改变。 AISI 和其他评估者得出以下三个教训：

  • 对互联网访问的更严格控制。 我们正在我们的网络范围中构建细粒度的网络控制，目的是在适当限制它们的同时保持这些评估所需的现实性。 我们已经在所有其他评估中使用了细粒度的网络控制，现在将把授予互联网访问权限的决定视为必须积极证明合理性的决定，而不是默认的决定。
  • 实时监控。 我们正在引入监控功能，用于在评估运行时对其进行监视，能够在发生超出范围的操作时对其进行标记或阻止。
  • 重新评估评估设计。 评估应假设一个有能力的模型可能会尝试超出其职权范围的行为，并且预先限制任何此类行为的范围。 AISI 的沙盒指南建议根据评估的设计定制沙盒配置；良好的遏制不应取决于模型选择不测试其边界。 我们还添加了额外的检查，以确保正确指定任务并可通过预期路线解决。

除了这些变化之外，我们还从网络安全和人工智能协调的角度分析发生的情况，并审核过去对可能被忽视的类似行为的评估。

我们也公开披露这一点，以便其他人可以学习我们的经验，并继续与 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 密切合作，进一步调查这一事件。

‍这对个人和企业意味着什么

该事件发生在受控评估中，而不是在普通使用中，并且在测试场景之外没有明确的迹象表明存在类似活动。 然而，这是一个需要做好准备的理由。 随着人工智能模型变得更加强大和易于使用，我们在这次事件中看到的情况可能会变得更加普遍。

最有效的应对措施仍然是标准的网络卫生，随着人工智能的进步，这一点变得更加重要。 组织应确保网络安全基础知识得到稳健实施，并在验证外部代码和贡献时保持谨慎。 这是五眼网络安全机构领导人联合呼吁采取行动的领域，国家网络安全中心也发布了如何随着前沿人工智能网络能力发展做好准备的指南。 我们鼓励各类组织注册 NCSC 的免费预警服务，将网络作为董事会级别的责任，并要求整个供应链都采用网络要素。

‍最终反思‍

此类事件反映出人工智能发展的速度。 随着能力的进步，了解这些系统并确保其安全的工作必须与它们同步。

AISI 是一个有能力的组织，拥有强大的安全实践，我们通过自己的程序识别了这种行为。 但没有任何组织的防御措施能够无限期地保持充分。 在这种情况下，我们故意启用了互联网访问，并且没有主动监控，这样行为就会更快地浮出水面——我们将直接解决这些问题。 我们对这些教训持开放态度，以便其他人可以学习和调整。

与 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 最近报告的事件一起来看，这一事件表明风险格局发生了变化。 不仅当人们故意滥用公开可用的模型时，而且当有能力的代理人在内部研究或特权访问环境中采取超出其授权范围的意外行动时，也可能会造成伤害。

我们概述了与此事件相关的重要警告。 这些行为是在智能体试图完成任务的评估过程中出现的。 我们目前无法确定智能体何时认为自己处于测试中，或者如何意识到其行为对现实世界的潜在影响。 无论如何，这一事件表明了一个值得立即关注的方向。

AISI 的存在是为了识别这些问题、理解它们并分享我们所学到的知识，以便在部署更强大的系统之前解决这些问题——在人工智能实验室内部、向值得信赖的合作伙伴以及公众。 这项工作尚未完成，但已在政府、行业和研究界共享。 当前的任务是强化防御，确保安全工作跟上。
